prompt:
Find what the PostgreSQL Global Development Group officially states about how long each major PostgreSQL version receives fixes. Cite the official versioning policy page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
According to the official PostgreSQL documentation, the PostgreSQL Global Development Group provides support (in the form of fixes) for each major version for a period of five years.

The policy is detailed on the Versioning Policy page of the PostgreSQL website. The key statement regarding the support duration is as follows.

SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ | QUOTE: "PostgreSQL major versions are supported for five years after their initial release." | CLAIM: The official support period for receiving fixes for a major PostgreSQL version is five years.

The page further clarifies the nature of the support, which is specifically limited to bug fixes and security issues, not new features.

SOURCE: https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ | QUOTE: "A major version is indicated by increasing either the first or second part of the version number, e.g. 9.4 to 9.5 or 9.5 to 10. During the five year support period, the community will release minor versions containing bug fixes and security issues for that major version." | CLAIM: Support for a major version means the release of minor versions that contain bug and security fixes.
